answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to make every new identity pay a real compute cost first. Each agent solves a fresh proof of work, so a thousand fake accounts cost a thousand proofs. Peers then check each other's answers, and rewards go only to work other agents attest as coherent. Trust builds slowly, like a climb to the summit, and new challenges arrive at dawn each epoch, so a farm of duplicate agents must keep paying for compute while honest agents keep earning. The echo of those costs is what makes spam expensive.
